summary: Target-level continuation of the accepted predecessor. Reuse every existing character, sum, lifting, Stickelberger and convention node. Supply actual field-coordinate Fourier transport and its trivial boundary; give the missing BFP two-point interpolation target; specify digit-factorial distribution and a public exact-Gamma route to Hasse–Davenport, retaining its two analytic supplier obligations. Include the elementary Gauss comparison for a presented product of finite fields. This is a completed planning pass, not gap-free source closure or formalisation.

nodes.title: Fourier inversion and Parseval in field coordinates
nodes.statement: Put e(a)=ψ.mulShift a, so e(a)(x)=ψ(ax). With C_f(a)=(AddChar.complexBasis F).repr(f)(e(a)), for every f,g:F→ℂ and x∈F simultaneously ∑a C_f(a)ψ(ax)=f(x) and q⁻¹∑y f(y)conj(g(y))=∑a C_f(a)conj(C_g(a)). Here C_f(a)=q⁻¹∑y f(y)conj(ψ(ay)).
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
ψ is primitive; over a field this means ψ is nontrivial.
proofSteps: Use the predecessor additive-characters-are-shifts bijection a↦ψ_a on the actual additive group (F,+). Native shift injectivity and AddChar.card_eq verify both domain and dual cardinality q. Construct a local indexing equivalence from that bijection; do not define a second dual object.

Import AC.0/fourier-transform and its fourier_eq_basis_repr and fourier_inversion_reindex APIs. Reindex the dual sum by e. The normalization is q⁻¹ on the transform only, and the inversion kernel has positive sign ψ(ax).
Import AC.0/fourier-parseval and apply the same bijection to both coefficients. This proves the simultaneous identities without using a cyclic Fourier transform or an equivalence with ZMod q.
acceptance: For δ_b, C(a)=q⁻¹conj(ψ(ab)); inversion gives δ_b and Parseval gives q⁻¹. For f=1 only a=0 survives with coefficient 1.
Use F₄: its additive group is (Z/2Z)², so a cyclic ZMod 4 transform cannot satisfy this character parametrisation.

Assembly replaces the predecessor Fourier node’s coarse AC.0 edge by the two exact owner node ids and this transport; its old general-Fourier request is discharged. No predecessor file is edited in this part.

sources.match: The finite-field specialization and field-coordinate reindexing of the already owned general Fourier identities.

nodes.title: Fourier coefficients with the trivial-character boundary
nodes.statement: For every χ and a∈F, C_χ(a)=q⁻¹∑x χ(x)conj(ψ(ax)) equals (q−1)/q if a=0 and χ=1, equals 0 if a=0 and χ≠1, and equals q⁻¹χ⁻¹(−a)g(χ,ψ) if a≠0.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
proofSteps: Use the owner Fourier definition and its native-basis-coordinate comparison. Complex additive character conjugation replaces ψ(ax) by ψ(−ax).
For a=0 use MulChar.sum_eq_zero_of_ne_one or MulChar.sum_one_eq_card_units. A field has q−1 units; its trivial character is not the constant function 1 on F.

For a≠0 use the unit −a in gaussSum_mulShift_eq. This covers χ=1 as well: g(1,ψ)=−1, hence nonzero coefficients are −1/q. For χ≠1 it agrees with the predecessor’s existing expansion, so assembly keeps that older target and adds the boundary API.
acceptance: For χ=1 and a=0 the answer is (q−1)/q, not 0.
For χ=1 and a≠0 the answer is −1/q; inversion recovers 0 at x=0 and 1 at every unit.
For a nontrivial χ, a=0 gives 0; the sign in χ⁻¹(−a) is tested by δ and the chosen ψ, rather than absorbed into a changed transform convention.

nodes.title: Distribution of digit sums and digit factorials
nodes.statement: Let M=p^f−1, d=M/m, s(r)=the sum of native base-p digits and h(r)=the product of their factorials (h(0)=1). For 0≤b<d, ∑_{0≤j<m}s(b+jd)=s(mb)+∑_{1≤j<m}s(jd). In ZMod p, m^{s(mb)}∏_{0≤j<m}h(b+jd)=h(mb)∏_{1≤j<m}h(jd).
hypotheses: p is prime, f>0, m>0 and m divides M. Thus M>0, d>0 and p∤m. No odd-prime restriction.
proofSteps: Pad each digit list to length f. Multiplication by p modulo M cycles the digits for r<M; s(r)=(p−1)∑_{i<f}{p^i r/M}. For each i, multiplication by p^i permutes j modulo m. The elementary fractional-part distribution on this grid gives the first identity after summation over i. All arguments b+jd and mb lie in [0,M).

For b>0 put k=mb, so 0<k<M. Import L3/gross-koblitz-source-multiplication-theorem with its actual Morita Gamma and positive fractional preimages. The numerator preimages, after permuting j for each i, are the cyclic fractions for b+jd; denominators are those for mb and jd, 1≤j<m. None is an integer here, so positive versus ordinary fractional parts agree.

Reduce that exact Gamma identity modulo p using L3/morita-gamma-sharp-reduction at precision 1 and its recurrence. If r has low digit r₀, r/M≡−r₀ mod p and Γ_p(r/M)≡Γ_p(−r₀)=1/r₀!; all factorials are units since r₀<p. Multiplying over the cyclic rotations gives 1/h(r). The Teichmuller value reduces to m^k. Since k≡s(k) mod p−1, rearrangement gives the stated factorial product.

For b=0 both identities are tautologies after splitting off the j=0 term; do not insert Gamma(1) for Gamma(0). At p=2 every digit factorial and m in ZMod 2 is 1; this congruence is valid but by itself cannot identify a binary root of unity.
acceptance: p=5,f=1,m=2,b=1: the factorial congruence is 2²·1!·3! ≡2!·2!≡4 modulo 5, detecting an inverted m exponent.
p=3,f=2,m=2,b=1: the sum identity is s(1)+s(5)=1+3= s(2)+s(4)=2+2; factorial identity gives 2²·1·2=2·1 modulo 3.
b=0 and m=1 are exact boundary cases. The binary factorial test is tautological and is not the product-theorem proof.

sources.locator: §11.7.4, Lemma 11.7.14 and proof of Corollary 11.7.15, pp.392–394; Gamma distribution Theorem 11.6.14, pp.372–375
sources.match: Cyclic Gamma distribution and digit-sum cancellation. The source cites Vol.I Proposition 3.7.1; the fractional-part derivation and reduction above supply the requested digit/factorial interface without claiming to have read the unavailable Vol.I proof.

nodes.title: Completion of the Hasse–Davenport product plan
nodes.statement: For all χ, g(χ^m,ψ)∏_{1≤j<m}g(ρ^j,ψ)=χ(m)^m∏_{0≤j<m}g(χρ^j,ψ). This is the unconditional target; the proof plan has the explicit Dwork supplier gap below.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
m>0 divides q−1; ρ has exact order m; ψ is primitive. In particular m is a unit in F. χ may be trivial, χ^m may be trivial, and p may be 2.
proofSteps: For m=1 the identity is immediate. Choose a generator ω of the multiplicative character group, with the predecessor’s Teichmuller/prime-above-p convention. Write ρ=ω^{−td}, gcd(t,m)=1, d=(q−1)/m, and χ=ω^{−a}. Permuting j removes t; replacing a by its residue b mod d permutes the numerator and leaves χ^m and χ(m)^m unchanged.

If b=0, χ is a power of ρ, so the numerator is a permutation of all ρ^j factors. As a is a multiple of d, χ^m=1 and χ(m)^m=1. Use g(1,ψ)=−1 to split off the j=0 factor. This case avoids the excluded exponent q−1 endpoint.

For 0<b<d first use the canonical trace character. Compare all character values inside their cyclotomic coefficient field and its completion at the predecessor’s chosen prime above p, and then transport through an injective complex embedding. Invoke L3/robert-gross-koblitz-comparison ONLY with the actual coefficient-bound and chosen-root splitting inputs requested from RD.6. It gives the source-negative sum −g(ω^{-r},ψ)=π^{s(r)}∏_{i<f}Γ_p(e(r,i)), with compatible π^{p−1}=−p, for 0≤r<q−1. Use the maximal-ideal chosen-root normalization printed in Cohen Lemma 11.7.12: its modulus is the fraktur prime ideal 𝔭, not the rational integer p. The alleged source error E750 is rejected by independent review.

Apply digit-product-distribution to cancel the π powers. The exact L3 Gamma multiplication quotient, with k=mb, equals ω(m)^{mb}=χ(m)^{−m}. There are m source-negative sums on each side, so their signs cancel. Multiplication by χ(m)^m gives the target. This exact prime-to-p Teichmuller identity replaces the predecessor’s insufficient inference from a congruence modulo the cyclotomic prime.

L3 identifies the Gamma quotient by proving its normalized (p−1)st power is 1 and its residue is 1; reduction is injective on these prime-to-p roots. For p=2 the exponent p−1 is 1, so the equality is exact before reduction. No claim that an arbitrary p-power root congruent to 1 must be trivial is used.

For arbitrary primitive ψ, use the predecessor shift parametrisation and gaussSum_mulShift_eq. Both sides acquire the same χ^{-m}(u)∏_{1≤j<m}ρ^{-j}(u) factor. All Gauss factors are nonzero by the native nontrivial theorem or the trivial value −1. This route is arithmetic and p-adic analytic; it does not use étale cohomology or Poincare duality.
acceptance: m=1 gives gχ=gχ, including χ=1.
If χ is any power of ρ, both sides agree by permutation and g1=−1, including χ^m=1.
At q=4,m=3 and a character ρ of order 3, χ=ρ gives −gρ gρ² on both sides. This tests characteristic two and the j=0 sign.

The factorial congruence alone leaves a possible p-power root; the exact Gamma quotient is the required stronger equality. The Dwork assumptions have not been discharged, so this node is planned, not closed.
Assembly retains predecessor /hasse-davenport-product-relation as the target and attaches this completion route; no duplicate target or second planet is promoted.

nodes.title: Evaluation of a prescribed-degree binary form
nodes.statement: For d≥0 and x:Option F define an F-linear map E_d(x):Polynomial.degreeLT F(d+1)→F. E_d(some a,P)=P(a), E_d(none,P)=coeff_d(P). Option F labels the standard representatives [a:1] and [1:0]. It is the evaluation of ∑_{i≤d}coeff_i(P)X^i Z^{d−i} in these representatives, not a coordinate-independent scalar on arbitrary representatives.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
The ambient degree d is part of the data, even when degree P<d.
proofSteps: Use the existing native degreeLT submodule; compose its inclusion with Polynomial.leval a at finite points and Polynomial.lcoeff F d at infinity. These are already linear maps, so the constructor has the required algebraic structure.
For the homogeneous interpretation substitute (a,1) or (1,0) in the displayed degree-d homogenization. No projective-space or binary-form carrier is introduced.

The native coefficient equivalence gives the monomial formula. Addition and scalar compatibility are native linear-map laws; the degree-lowering assertion follows from coefficient vanishing. These routine API computations stay inside this target-level node.
acceptance: Each of the five named tests is included as an example in the suggested file.
Changing representatives by λ≠0 scales the section value by λ^d. Consequently the fixed chart is stated explicitly; no canonical scalar evaluation on P¹ is asserted.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.2 proof, arXiv v2 pp.8–9, the sums over P¹(F_q) and over all polynomials of degree at most d
sources.match: Makes the implicit prescribed-degree homogenization at infinity precise. The small interpolation API is the finite-field consumer of native polynomial evaluation, not a new general interpolation theory.

nodes.title: Uniform two-evaluation fibres
nodes.statement: For d≥1 and distinct x,y:Option F, the map P↦(E_d(x,P),E_d(y,P)) from Polynomial.degreeLT F(d+1) to F×F is surjective. For every u,v∈F its fibre has cardinality q^{d−1}.
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
proofSteps: Use Polynomial.degreeLTEquiv to identify a polynomial with its d+1 coefficients. This provides the finite enumeration, without defining another vector-space carrier.

If x=some a and y=some b, fix all coefficients except a₀,a₁. The two residual equations have determinant b−a≠0 and have a unique solution. The remaining d−1 coordinates give a bijection of each fibre with F^{d−1}.

If exactly one point is infinity, fix a_d to its prescribed value. Fix all coordinates except a₀,a_d, and solve a₀ from the finite evaluation. Again there are d−1 free coordinates. If infinity comes first, swap the two target coordinates.
Distinctness excludes the two-infinity case. The explicit coefficient bijections prove both existence and cardinality. No general multivariate or scheme interpolation theorem is required.
acceptance: At d=1 every fibre is a singleton, including the pair (some 0,none).
Over F₃ at d=2 the pair (some 0,none) has exactly 3 polynomials for each prescribed pair of values.
d=0 is excluded: constants give a diagonal image. x=y is excluded even for d≥1, since unequal prescribed values cannot be interpolated.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.2 proof, arXiv v2 pp.8–9, interpolation sentence
sources.match: Explicit uniform-fibre proof of the paper’s two-point interpolation step. d≥1 suffices for this ingredient; the source uses d≥2 in its subsequent induction.

nodes.title: Two-point character orthogonality for all polynomials
nodes.statement: For d≥1, x≠y and χ≠1, ∑_{P∈Polynomial.degreeLT F(d+1)}χ(E_d(x,P))φ(E_d(y,P))=0 for every φ. The accompanying declaration projectiveEval_character_correlation_all states the stronger identity, without χ≠1: this sum is q^{d−1}(∑uχ(u))(∑vφ(v)).
hypotheses: F is a finite field with q=#F; all additive and multiplicative characters take values in ℂ. Multiplicative characters, including 1, are zero on nonunits.
d≥1 and x,y:Option F are distinct. For vanishing χ is nontrivial; φ can be trivial. No monic or squarefree restriction and no conjugation in the product.
proofSteps: Partition the finite coefficient space by the two evaluation values. Use projective-two-evaluation-uniform to give every fibre multiplicity q^{d−1}.
Factor the double finite sum to obtain the all-character identity. Then apply the existing MulChar.sum_eq_zero_of_ne_one to χ. This supplies the target from the exact native row-orthogonality owner.

For the source’s odd-q quadratic character extend by zero and transport its integer values to ℂ. The sum vanishes for each ordered distinct pair, hence summing over those pairs gives the BFP interpolation total for d≥2. The squarefree induction and the hyperelliptic automorphism-weighted moment remain in the paper’s other owners.
acceptance: For χ=φ=1 the all-character sum is q^{d−1}(q−1)², so a zero claim without nontriviality is false.
For d=1, x=some 0 and y=none, coefficient pairs enumerate F² once and give (∑χ)(∑φ).
For odd q and its nontrivial quadratic χ, the all-polynomial distinct-pair total in BFP is zero. The theorem itself remains valid in characteristic two for any available nontrivial χ; F₂ has none.
Do not sum over squarefree or monic polynomials; those restrictions destroy the equal-fibre argument.

nodes.title: Gauss sums on products of finite fields
nodes.statement: Let ι be finite and K_i finite fields, A=∏_i K_i the native product ring. Given native characters χ:A→ℂ, ψ:A→ℂ and χ_i,ψ_i on K_i such that χ(x)=∏iχ_i(x_i) and ψ(x)=∏iψ_i(x_i) for all x, g_A(χ,ψ)=∏i g_{K_i}(χ_i,ψ_i).
hypotheses: The hypotheses explicitly give the component factorisations; arbitrary characters are not silently declared to factor. No primitivity or nontriviality is required. All Gauss sums use Mathlib’s native definition on finite commutative rings.
proofSteps: Unfold the native Gauss sum and insert the two character factorisations. Combine the component products to make the summand ∏i(χ_i(x_i)ψ_i(x_i)).
Apply Fintype.prod_sum in reverse. This proves the comparison even with trivial component characters and with an empty index set.

For a finite étale algebra already presented as a product of finite fields, norm-induced multiplicative and trace-induced additive characters have exactly these factorisations, by the component norm product and trace sum. Their component lifts are the predecessor’s existing norm/trace-lift objects. The theorem consumes a presentation; it does not construct or classify finite étale algebras.
acceptance: Two components give g_A=g_1g_2 with the native positive-sum sign.

Two nontrivial additive components and trivial multiplicative components give g_A=(−1)²=1, whereas the source-negative convention −g_A gives −1; an étale-algebra lifting sign must count the components explicitly.
An empty product is the singleton ring and both sides equal 1. The statement also permits zero Gauss factors.

checked.note: The native complex-basis coordinates equal the normalized AC.0 transform. Its inversion/reindexing and Parseval APIs, together with the predecessor primitive-shift bijection, supply the two identities on the actual additive group of F. This includes noncyclic extension fields.

Native zero extension gives the two zero-frequency cases. Complex conjugation changes the additive multiplier to −a; the native unit-shift theorem then gives χ⁻¹(−a), including the trivial-character value −1/q at nonzero frequencies.

Cohen’s cyclic Gamma distribution and the four exact L3 suppliers justify the digit-sum and factorial identities. Precision-one reduction applies also at p=2; b=0 and m=1 are separated. Independent exact enumeration passed 17517 cases, including 69 binary cases.

Conrad (A.6) and Cohen Theorem 11.7.16(1) support the exact intervals, multiplier and trivial-character exceptions. The exact Gamma quotient supplies the prime-to-p root identity, including p=2. The constructor composes the native degreeLT inclusion with leval or the ambient coefficient map lcoeff. Its six APIs and five discriminating tests match the corrected reader and elaborated suggested file; the fixed projective representatives and degree-zero boundary are explicit.

Solving two coefficient equations at distinct finite points, or the top and constant coefficients with infinity, yields both surjectivity and q^(d−1) fibres for d≥1. Independent enumeration passed 192 ordered-point/degree cases.

Uniform fibre counting followed by native multiplicative row sums proves the all-character identity and nontrivial vanishing. This supplies only BFP’s all-polynomial interpolation ingredient; its squarefree induction is outside this target.
